Title: IT Director, Identity & Directory Services (HYBRID)
Location: Mississauga, Ontario, Canada | Mississauga, ON, Canada
Industry: Food and Beverage Services, Food and Beverage Manufacturing, and Manufacturing
Description:
McCormick Canada continues its long track record of growth and is a respected leader in the spice, seasoning, flavouring and specialty food industry. Our consumer products division serves retail grocery customers and emerging channels with Club House, Billy Bee and McCormick products, while our Custom Flavour Solutions division serves food service distributors and other respected food manufacturers across Canada. McCormick Canada is part of the world leader in spice and seasonings, McCormick & Company Inc.
  
  
The Power of People is one of our five pillars. It has been the foundation for McCormick's success for decades. There is something inspiring about working at McCormick. We have created an unusually dedicated workforce by fostering a culture of respect, recognition, inclusion and collaboration based on the highest ethical values. Without our employees, our success is not possible. Our commitment to our customers, our consumers and our employees is unsurpassed.
  
  
**Position Overview**
The Director, Identity and Access Management (IAM) is responsible for defining and executing the global strategy for enterprise identity and access management and directory services at McCormick. This leader is accountable for secure, reliable and scalable access to business applications and technology platforms, including directory infrastructure, authentication, authorization, privileged access and identity lifecycle services.
  
  
The role leads modernization and automation of IAM capabilities across cloud and on-premises environments, strengthens identity-related controls in partnership with Cybersecurity, and drives a consistent, efficient employee and partner experience. The Director leads internal teams and managed service providers and maintains clear accountability for service performance, resilience and a multi-year modernization roadmap.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Define and execute the enterprise IAM and Directory services strategy, standards and roadmap aligned with business needs, Cybersecurity and Enterprise Architecture.
* As the Product Line leader for IAM and Directory Services, establish a 12–24-month modernization roadmap, simplifying legacy directory and authentication architecture and reducing technical debt.
* Lead engineering, delivery and lifecycle management of enterprise IAM services, including Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, hybrid directory services, SSO, MFA, federation, access provisioning and privileged access capabilities.
* Establish standardized identity and access patterns for applications, cloud services, employee, partner and non-human identities.
* Oversee platform resilience, recovery, change management, configuration standards and operational readiness.
* Drive IAM automation and access lifecycle improvement.
* Automate joiner, mover and leaver workflows, provisioning, deprovisioning, entitlement changes and access fulfillment through HR and service management integrations.
* Use APIs, scripting and repeatable engineering practices to reduce manual effort, improve accuracy and shorten fulfillment times.
* Partner with Cybersecurity to strengthen enterprise access controls and reduce risk.
* Advance least-privilege, privileged access management, identity governance, access reviews, service-account controls and audit readiness.
* Address vulnerabilities, control gaps and audit findings while balancing risk, usability and business continuity.
* Build and lead a high-performing global IAM and directory services organization.
* Direct internal teams and managed service providers; establish ownership, service levels, performance measures and continuous-improvement routines.
* Develop talent, manage vendor performance and collaborate with Digital Workplace, Cloud, Applications, HR and Service Management.
* Own IAM service economics, stakeholder communications and measurable delivery outcomes.
* Prioritize investments, manage budgets and licensing, report operational performance and guide adoption of enterprise IAM standards.

**Secondary Responsibilities**
Participate in enterprise architecture discussions, technology risk and change governance; support audits, disaster recovery exercises and major incidents involving IAM services. Evaluate emerging IAM capabilities and contribute to enterprise technology standards, service introduction and continuous improvement.
  
  
**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience
* Relevant technical certifications in Microsoft identity platforms, IAM, cloud or information security are beneficial.
* At least 10 years of progressive enterprise technology experience, including leadership in IAM, directory services, infrastructure or security-related engineering and operations.
* Demonstrated expertise with Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, hybrid identity, authentication, SSO, MFA, directory protocols and modern access management practices.
* Experience automating identity lifecycle processes, implementing access governance and privileged access capabilities, and managing services in complex global environments.
* Experience leading internal technical teams and managed service providers through operational improvement and platform modernization.
* Experience with IAM governance and privileged access platforms such as SailPoint, Saviynt, CyberArk or comparable technologies; familiarity with ServiceNow integrations.
* Experience modernizing legacy directories, implementing cloud-first identity architecture and supporting business integration or organizational transformation.
* Experience influencing senior leaders across regions and organizational boundaries, with demonstrated success leading large-scale change.

In the spirit of pay transparency, we are excited to share the base salary range for this position is $140,750-$190,750
  
  
Base salary compensation will be determined based on factors such as geographic location, skills, education, experience for this role, and/or internal equity of our current employees as part of any final offer. This position is also eligible to participate in
**McCormick’s Incentive Bonus (MIB) Plan**
. In addition to a competitive compensation package, permanent employees of McCormick Canada are eligible for our extensive Total Rewards programs that include:
  
  

+ Comprehensive health plans covering medical, vision, dental, life and disability benefits
+ Family-friendly benefits such as maternity leave top-up and Employee Assistance Program
+ Retirement and investment programs including a matching DC pension plan, group RRSP, and Employee Stock Purchase Plan

This posting is for a new position within McCormick.
  
  
Please note that McCormick does not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the recruitment process.

Title: Manager, Digital Practice
Description:
R.V. Anderson Associates (RVA) is a proudly Canadian‑owned consulting engineering firm with 78 years of experience shaping the future that defines our communities across the country. With approximately 500 employees in 11 offices nationwide, RVA delivers integrated, multi‑disciplinary engineering expertise across five provinces.

Our practice is founded on a strong set of values that unite people, projects, and the planet. Guided by these principles, RVA fosters a collaborative, high performance culture where technical excellence, environmental responsibility, and professional development are integral to our work. We are dedicated to investing in our people, promoting knowledge sharing, and delivering sustainable engineering solutions that create meaningful, lasting impact for communities—now and for future generations.

RVA is looking for an experienced Manager, Digital Practice who will be responsible for CAD and BIM standards, the engineering application portfolio, automation, and digital workflows used in project execution.

The Manager, Digital Practice leads this function and advances the firm’s digital delivery capability. The role requires combined engineering delivery and technology experience, current knowledge of AI and automation capability applicable to professional engineering practice, and the ability to work effectively with both engineering and IT stakeholders.

Based out of any of our Ontario offices, the successful candidate will be reporting directly to RVA’s Vice President, Information Technology & Information Management.

**Duties:**

**Digital Delivery Strategy**

* Own and advance the firm’s digital practice roadmap, including CAD and BIM maturity, model-based delivery, common data environment, and asset-data capability, with defined sequencing and outcomes.
* Advise pursuit teams and practice leaders on digital delivery requirements in RFPs and client specifications, including BIM execution plans and ISO 19650 or client-specific information management requirements.
* Benchmark the firm’s digital delivery capability against peers and client expectations in the municipal, water and wastewater, transportation, and infrastructure sectors, and recommend investment priorities.

**Engineering Application Portfolio and Standards**

* Own the engineering application portfolio, including Autodesk AEC products, Bentley products, hydraulic and process modelling tools, and GIS, covering standards, configuration, upgrade cycles, and license management.
* Maintain CAD and BIM standards, templates, content libraries, and title blocks, and ensure they are current, documented, and consistently applied across offices and disciplines.
* Establish model and drawing quality management practices, including data integrity checks, model audits, and management of legacy content.
* Define digital deliverable quality control requirements with discipline leads, recognizing that engineering sign-off remains with the practitioners of record.
* Manage software vendor and reseller relationships, including renewals, support performance, and roadmap commitments.

**AI and Emerging Technology in Engineering Practice**

* Identify, evaluate, pilot, and scale AI and automation capability in engineering workflows, including design assistance, document and specification review, quantity and drawing extraction, model checking, retrieval over project history, and task automation.
* Operate within the firm’s AI governance framework, including the sanctioned tool list, generative AI policy and procedure, and AI deployment strategy, and bring proposals forward through that process.
* Assess emerging tools against professional obligations, practice requirements, documentation and record retention triggers, professional liability exposure, and restrictions on AI use.
* Validate vendor capability claims through structured evaluation prior to adoption.
* Build staff capability through training, written guidance, and a network of digital champions across offices and disciplines.

**Automation, Data, and Integration**

* Direct development of automation that reduces repetitive production effort, using Dynamo, LISP, .NET and other APIs, PowerShell, Power Platform, and scripted model and data auditing.
* Collaborate on standards for documentation, version control, testing, support, and retirement of internally developed tools.
* Work with the IT/IM team to enhance integration between engineering tools and core business systems, linking corporate datasets.
* Ensure engineering content is created and stored in a manner that supports the firm’s managed content platform, retention obligations, and downstream search and retrieval.

**Leadership**

* Lead, develop, and set Digital Practice priorities.
* Manage the Digital Practice budget, including software licensing, training, and initiative expenditure.
* Lead the CAD/BIM process improvement committee.
* Represent Digital Practice to leadership, practice leaders, and project managers, and report on capability, adoption, and results.
* Other related duties as assigned/required and appropriate to this position.

**Qualifications:**

**Required**

* Degree in engineering, or an engineering technology diploma with equivalent practice experience.
* Eight or more years of combined engineering delivery and technology experience, including at least three years in a leadership or digital practice role.
* Production experience in a consulting engineering, architecture, or construction environment, including development and checking of project deliverables.
* Good working knowledge of CAD and BIM platforms and standards including template, content, and reference management at an enterprise level.
* Familiarity with application of AI or advanced automation to professional or technical workflows.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present to executive audiences.

**Preferred**

* P.Eng., C.E.T., or equivalent professional designation.
* Experience in municipal infrastructure, water and wastewater, or transportation sectors.
* Familiarity with ISO 19650, BIM execution planning, and public-sector digital delivery specifications.
* Scripting or development capability in Dynamo, Python, .NET, PowerShell, or LISP sufficient to prototype and to review the work of others.
* Experience with enterprise content platforms, common data environments, or GIS integration.
* Exposure to AI governance, professional liability, or regulatory practice requirements in a licensed engineering context.

**Your better starts here**

We don’t settle for less, and neither should you. As it happens, offering great benefits to our people is entirely possible: the numbers work out. Happy teams mean happy clients. It’s just that simple. From recruitment to flexibility, learning to leadership, wellness to inclusion, we give our people the tools they need to outperform in their careers and build lasting connections with our clients, our culture, and each other.

Title: Regional Operations Manager
Company: Splash N Learn Swim School Inc
Description:
**Locations:** All Splash N’ Learn locations, currently Barrie and Vaughan, Ontario

**Position:** Full-Time | Multi-Location

**Reports To:** Owners

**Salary:** $ 80, 000– 90,000 annually

**A Bit About Us**

At Splash N’ Learn, we take swimming seriously and believe learning should be fun. We help

swimmers build confidence, develop essential water safety skills, and feel proud of their progress

in a warm, welcoming environment.

With locations in Barrie and Vaughan, we’re building a business where families feel welcome, staff

feel supported, and leaders take pride in what they do. Behind every great lesson is a team that

communicates well, works together, has FUN and cares about getting the details right.

As we grow, we’re looking for someone who brings that same combination of care, energy, and

follow-through to leading our facilities.

**The Opportunity**

We’re looking for a Regional Operations Manager who is **great with people and great at getting** **things done.**

Reporting to the Owners, you’ll lead and develop our Facility Managers, strengthen daily

operations, drive enrollment and retention, and improve financial performance across our

locations.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll spend time in our facilities, get to know the teams,

observe what’s working, and turn challenges into practical improvements. Some days that means

coaching a manager through a difficult conversation. Other days it means reviewing staffing costs,

improving registration follow-up, or developing a creative way to connect with local families.

You’ll bring structure where it’s needed, build on what’s working, and help our teams plan ahead.

You’ll also develop the systems, staffing models, and leadership capacity needed to support future

growth.

**Your goal: strong teams, confident managers, happy families, and well-run facilities that**

**can succeed independently.**

**Who You Are**

**You know how to lead people.**

You understand that different people need different approaches. You listen, read the room, and

adjust your communication while keeping expectations clear. You can give honest feedback,

navigate difficult conversations, and hold people accountable while maintaining their trust.

**You bring high emotional intelligence.**

You’re self-aware, thoughtful, and composed under pressure. You’re curious about other

perspectives and willing to reflect on your own approach. People feel comfortable coming to you

and trust you to address what needs attention.

**You bring energy and personality.**

You’re approachable, down-to-earth, and enjoy connecting with people. You know when humour,

encouragement, or a fresh idea can make a difference. You help create a workplace where people

enjoy coming to work and take pride in doing a great job.

**You’re organized and thorough.**

You notice the details, keep track of commitments, and close the loop. Meetings lead to action,

plans have clear owners, and important tasks don’t disappear when the next busy day arrives.

**You’re a great communicator.**

Whether you’re coaching a manager, speaking with a parent, or updating leadership, you make

things easy to understand. You share information proactively, set clear expectations, and address

concerns directly and respectfully.

**You’re creative and practical.**

You enjoy finding better ways to do things. You can turn a good idea into a workable plan, bring

others along, and follow it through to completion.

**You understand the business.**

You’re comfortable with budgets, staffing costs, enrollment, and performance reports. You use that

information to make thoughtful decisions and help managers understand how their daily choices

affect results.

**You love seeing others grow.**

You’re willing to step in and help, and you make time to teach, delegate, and build confidence.

You take pride in seeing managers take ownership, solve problems, and become stronger

leaders.

**What You’ll Be Responsible For**

**Leadership & Manager Development**

Our Facility Managers will look to you for direction, coaching, and support. A major part of your

success will be helping them become confident, capable leaders. This role requires regular travel between facilities and flexibility to work evenings and weekends to support our teams during key operating hours.

* Provide direct leadership, mentorship, and ongoing development to Facility Managers.
* Establish clear responsibilities, performance expectations, and measurable goals.
* Lead regular one-on-one meetings, leadership check-ins, and performance reviews.
* Develop individualized leadership development plans and provide hands-on coaching where needed.
* Strengthen managers’ communication, delegation, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.
* Address performance concerns promptly and respectfully, with clear improvement plans and follow-up.
* Build managers’ ability to resolve routine issues and run daily operations independently.
* Identify and develop future leaders within our teams.

**Operations & Quality Assurance**

Safety is the foundation of everything we do, and consistency is how families learn to trust us.

You’ll make sure every family gets the same safe, high-quality Splash N’ Learn experience, no

matter which pool they walk into.

  

* Oversee daily operational performance across all facilities.
* Maintain a regular, hands-on presence through facility visits, observations, and coaching.
* Monitor lesson quality, customer service, cleanliness, organization, safety, and professionalism.
* Be the guardian of the Splash N’ Learn brand, keeping our look, voice, and family experience consistent at every location.
* Conduct operational reviews and ensure improvement plans are completed.
* Develop and maintain practical procedures, checklists, and tools that teams can consistently use.
* Identify recurring problems and implement solutions that address their causes.
* Coordinate maintenance, repairs, and equipment needs with Facility Managers and approved service providers.
* Ensure adherence to company policies, aquatic safety standards, and applicable regulations.
* Guide teams through new systems and procedures with clear communication, training, and follow-up.

**Scheduling, Staffing & Team Development**

You’ll help managers put the right people and programming in place to serve families well and

operate efficiently.

* Oversee program and staffing schedules for accuracy, consistency, and effective use of pool space.
* Align class offerings with demand, swimmer progression, and business priorities.
* Monitor class capacity, waitlists, staffing levels, and labour utilization.
* Establish practical staffing and coverage models that maintain safety and service quality while managing costs.
* Support recruitment, onboarding, training, and professional development.
* Help managers plan ahead for absences, seasonal changes, and enrollment growth.
* Strengthen employee engagement and retention through clear expectations, recognition, and development opportunities.

**Financial Performance & Resource Management**

You’ll help each location understand its numbers and take meaningful action to improve results.

  

* Take accountability for operational and financial performance within approved budgets and delegated authority.
* Develop and manage operating budgets with the Director of Operations.
* Review financial reports and monitor revenue, labour costs, operating expenses, and profitability.
* Identify opportunities to improve productivity, reduce unnecessary spending, and use resources effectively.
* Oversee purchasing practices, inventory controls, and vendor relationships.
* Track key performance indicators, including enrolment, class utilization, retention, labour percentages, customer satisfaction, and profitability.
* Develop and follow through on action plans when results fall short of agreed targets.

**Enrolment, Sales & Business Development**

You’ll help teams confidently communicate the value of our programs and make it easy for

families to join and stay.

* Establish consistent inquiry, registration, and follow-up practices across locations.
* Coach managers and customer service teams on recommending suitable programs, addressing questions, and closing registrations.
* Improve lead tracking, re-enrolment, and processes for welcoming new families.
* Collaborate with marketing on campaigns and promotions aligned with available capacity.
* Build relationships with schools, community organizations, and potential partners.
* Identify opportunities for new programs, local outreach, and sustainable revenue growth.
* Use customer feedback, local demand, and competitor insights to inform recommendations.

**Growth & New Locations**

We’re just getting started, and you’ll help bring the Splash N’ Learn experience to more families in

more communities.

When it’s time to open new doors, you’ll make sure each location feels like Splash N’ Learn from day one.

* Support future openings, acquisitions, or expansion projects as directed, from staffing and systems to training and operational readiness.
* Build repeatable opening playbooks, checklists, and onboarding plans so every new location launches with a strong team and our standards in place.
* Develop leaders from within who are ready to step up and run new facilities.
* Make sure every new location lives our values and our brand, so families get the same safe, fun Splash N’ Learn experience everywhere.
* Partner with the Owners on expansion priorities, timelines, and resources.

**Customer Experience & Retention**

Families are the heart of Splash N’ Learn, and you’ll keep their experience at the centre of every operational decision.

  

* Ensure service is welcoming, responsive, and consistent across locations.
* Coach Facility Managers through escalated concerns while strengthening their ability to handle future situations.
* Monitor feedback, withdrawals, and retention trends to identify opportunities for improvement.
* Address recurring concerns through changes to training, communication, or processes.
* Ensure families receive clear information about programming, swimmer progress, policies, and registration.
* Help teams build positive relationships that give families confidence in choosing Splash N’ Learn.

**Safety & Business Continuity**

Safety comes first. Always. You’ll make sure our teams are prepared, trained, and ready to

respond with confidence when the unexpected happens.

* Ensure emergency procedures, incident reporting practices, and required training remain current.
* Support managers in identifying hazards and completing corrective actions.
* Monitor required staff qualifications, certifications, and training records.
* Maintain practical plans for staffing shortages, equipment failures, and facility interruptions.
* Ensure critical supplies, equipment, and service arrangements are in place.
* Escalate significant safety, staffing, financial, or facility concerns promptly to the Director of Operations.

**Communication & Accountability**

Integrity means doing what we say we’ll do. You’ll keep people informed, priorities clear, and

commitments moving forward.

* Serve as the primary operational support and escalation contact for Facility Managers.
* Provide regular updates to the Director of Operations on results, priorities, risks, and progress.
* Establish useful meeting routines, reporting expectations, and follow-up processes.
* Bring forward concerns with thoughtful recommendations and proposed next steps.
* Collaborate with leadership to align facility priorities with broader business goals.
* Make decisions within company policies, approved budgets, and delegated authority.
* Model ownership, professionalism, and consistent follow-through.

**What You Bring**

**Required Qualifications**

* At least five years of progressive management experience in a service-based organization.
* Demonstrated experience developing managers, leading multiple teams, or overseeing

multiple locations.

* Strong people-management skills, emotional intelligence, and the ability to build trust while

maintaining accountability.

* Experience managing budgets, reviewing profit and loss statements, and using

performance metrics to guide decisions.

* A record of improving operational efficiency, customer experience, or business results.
* Excellent communication, organization, problem-solving, and follow-through.
* Experience implementing procedures, training programs, and performance management

processes.

* Confidence using various technologies, and learning registration, scheduling, and

operational software.

* Ability to travel regularly between locations.
* Flexibility to work evenings and weekends as needed to observe operations, coach teams,

and support key priorities.

**Experience That Would Be an Asset**

* Experience in aquatics, fitness, recreation, hospitality, childcare, retail, or another

multi-location service business.

* Success improving enrolment, sales conversion, customer retention, and community

partnerships.

* Experience supporting new locations, business expansion, or operational transitions.
* Familiarity with iClassPro or similar registration and scheduling software
* Post-secondary education in business, operations, recreation, or a related field.

**Aquatics experience is an asset, but it is not required.**

**Strong leadership, operational** **management, and people-development experience are essential.**

**What Success Looks Like**

* Facility Managers confidently lead their teams and independently manage daily operations.
* Families experience consistent, high-quality lessons and customer service.
* Enrolment, class utilization, sales conversion, and retention improve.
* Labour costs and operating expenses stay within agreed targets.
* Teams use clear, practical systems and follow through on commitments.
* Recurring issues decrease, and managers resolve routine concerns with less senior leadership involvement.
* Staff feel supported, understand expectations, and have opportunities to grow.
* Facilities deliver stronger results and are prepared for sustainable growth..

**Compensation & Benefits**

* **Annual salary of $80,000-90,000**, based on qualifications and experience.
* Health benefits and paid vacation in accordance with company policy and the formal

employment agreement.

* Opportunities for professional growth and leadership development within a growing

organization.

**Sound Like You?**

If you love developing people, bringing order to a busy environment, and making a business

better, we’d love to hear from you.

Tell us about your leadership experience, what draws you to Splash N’ Learn, and an example of

how you helped a manager or team grow. We’re interested in both the results you achieved and

how you brought people along.

Title: Manager, Information Security Risk
Description:
**Company Summary**
===================

Come work for a company that’s committed to the success of each and every employee. A place where innovators and collaborators come together and build on each other’s talents. Where diversity is welcomed and celebrated.

FCT provides industry-leading title insurance, default solutions and other real estate related products and services to legal, lending, valuation and real estate professionals across Canada. With FCT, you will have the opportunity to build a meaningful career. Join us as we continue to do exciting work and make a big impact on our colleagues, customers and communities.

**Job Summary**
===============

We are continually searching for great talent; individuals who possess a deep commitment to the customers and markets we serve. If you would like to join a company that is committed to the success of each employee and offers challenge, purpose and the opportunity to grow both personally and professionally in a team-oriented environment, you'll enjoy a career with us! We understand that fostering a diverse and inclusive environment is critical for the success of our business, and we actively work towards it every day.

As the Manager, Information Security Risk, you will lead the assessment, governance, and oversight of information security risks across enterprise technology initiatives, with a primary focus on the secure adoption and enablement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions.  
  
This role is accountable for leading Threat Risk Assessments, AI security reviews, vendor and solution risk assessments, and architecture risk reviews to ensure technology initiatives are designed and implemented in alignment with FCT’s security standards, privacy obligations, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite.  
  
You will serve as a key Information Security advisor to business leaders, technology teams, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, Enterprise Architecture, and project delivery teams. The role will help establish practical guardrails, control expectations, and governance processes that enable responsible AI adoption while protecting FCT’s data, systems, customers, employees, and business operations.  
  
Working closely with the Director, Information Security & IT Risk, this role will support the continued maturation of FCT’s information security risk management program, including AI security governance, emerging technology risk assessment, regulatory alignment, security policy development, and enterprise risk reporting.

**HERE’S HOW YOU’LL CONTRIBUTE:**

* Lead Threat Risk Assessments for enterprise technology initiatives, including AI, Generative AI, machine learning, cloud, SaaS, and third-party technology solutions.
* Serve as the Information Security lead for AI-related initiatives, assessing risks related to data exposure, prompt injection, model misuse, third-party AI providers, data residency, retention, intellectual property, and regulatory obligations.
* Develop and maintain AI security standards, assessment methodologies, risk review processes, and practical guardrails to support responsible AI adoption across the organization.
* Review solution architectures, data flows, access models, and integration patterns to identify security risks and recommend appropriate control requirements.
* Partner with Legal, Privacy, Compliance, Enterprise Architecture, Procurement, Technology, and business stakeholders to assess and manage information security risks throughout the solution lifecycle.
* Track security findings and risk treatment activities through remediation, ensuring clear ownership, risk acceptance, escalation, and reporting where required.
* Monitor emerging AI, cyber, regulatory, and technology risk trends and provide recommendations to strengthen FCT’s security governance, policies, and control environment.

**HERE’S WHAT YOU’LL BRING:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Risk Management, or a related field, with 7+ years of experience in information security, technology risk, security architecture, governance, or a related discipline.
* Strong experience leading Threat Risk Assessments, security reviews, vendor risk assessments, solution risk assessments, or architecture reviews for enterprise technology initiatives.
* Solid understanding of information security controls across identity and access management, cloud security, data protection, logging and monitoring, secure architecture, third-party risk, and incident response.
* Experience assessing risks related to AI, Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise, Azure OpenAI, machine learning platforms, automation, or AI-enabled SaaS solutions is strongly preferred.
* Knowledge of security, privacy, and risk frameworks such as ISO 27001, NIST, SOC 2, PCI DSS, OWASP, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and applicable Canadian privacy and regulatory expectations.
* Strong ability to translate technical and security risks into clear business risk statements, practical recommendations, and executive-level summaries.
* Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders, challenge assumptions constructively, and enable business outcomes while maintaining appropriate security and governance standards.
* Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CCSP, ISO 27001, or AI/security-related certifications are considered an asset.

Title: IT Operations Sr. Manager
Description:
**POSITION SUMMARY:**
The Senior Manager, IT Operations is accountable for the strategy, performance, and continuous improvement of enterprise and field technology support. The role leads the Enterprise Service Desk, Field Services, end-user support, workplace technology, and assigned IT service management functions.
  
  
Serving both corporate and midstream operations, this leader builds strong teams, establishes clear accountability, and delivers reliable, secure, and cost-effective services across office, field, and operational environments.
  
  
**JOB DUTIES & KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Enterprise Service Desk & Corporate Support

+ Own the Enterprise Service Desk as the central point for intake, triage, communication, and escalation across corporate and field operations.
+ Own the executive support function, including service standards, coverage, escalation, communications, and coordination for senior leadership and executive meetings.
+ Set service levels, staffing, quality standards, operating procedures, and performance measures for corporate business functions, executives, and 24x7 field operations.
+ Integrate Service Desk, corporate support, executive support, and Field Services workflows to eliminate delays, duplicate effort, and weak handoffs.
+ Improve first-contact resolution, fulfillment speed, self-service, knowledge use, and support for office-based, executive, remote, and operationally critical users.

* Field Operations Leadership & IT/OT Partnership

+ Lead Field Services across pipelines, terminals, plants, field offices, remote facilities, control environments, and the mobile workforce.
+ Set regional coverage, remote-support, and escalation models for operationally critical locations.
+ Align support with operational priorities, safety requirements, site access, work permits, outage windows, and maintenance schedules.
+ Establish clear ownership and handoffs across IT, Field Operations, and OT.
+ Lead technology support for new facilities, expansions, acquisitions, site moves, construction, turnarounds, and OT deployments.
+ Maintain field-support readiness for severe weather, emergency response, and business continuity events.

* Service Operations & Major Incident Leadership

+ Own end-to-end support performance across Service Desk, Field Services, executive support, and workplace technology.
+ Coordinate the support organization’s response to major incidents affecting workforce productivity or field operations, supporting escalation, stakeholder communication, service restoration, and post-incident review.
+ Partner closely with Infrastructure, Server, Network, Cybersecurity, Cloud, and Enterprise Applications teams to coordinate support activities, drive service improvements, and resolve complex operational issues.
+ Use operating metrics to expose trends, aging work, repeat incidents, service risk, and capacity constraints.

* Endpoint, Mobility & Workplace Technology Operations

+ Own endpoint support, provisioning, refresh, mobility, collaboration, conferencing, printing, and workplace technology services across corporate and field environments.
+ Ensure workplace technology and field devices fit business requirements, environmental conditions, mobility, limited connectivity, and operational work patterns.
+ Oversee onboarding, offboarding, deployment, recovery, break/fix, warranty, and secure disposition.
+ Partner with endpoint engineering, cybersecurity, application owners, and business leaders to improve security, reliability, standardization, and supportability.
+ Maintain inventory accuracy and asset tracking across corporate offices, field locations, warehouses, and remote facilities.
+ Establish and enforce cycle-count standards, investigate variances, and drive timely reconciliation and corrective action.

* IT Service Management & Continuous Improvement

+ Manage assigned Incident, Request, Problem, Knowledge, Service Level, and Continual Improvement practices.
+ Apply ITIL foundations and relevant industry practices to improve service consistency, accountability, and outcomes without unnecessary administrative burden.
+ Use operational data, customer feedback, root-cause analysis, and lessons learned to set priorities and measure results.
+ Maintain a service improvement roadmap tied to business priorities, operational risk, and measurable outcomes.
+ Drive automation, self-service, AI-assisted support, remote support, workflow optimization, and knowledge management where they improve service, speed, or cost.

* People Leadership & Decision Making

+ Build and develop high-performing Service Desk and Field Services teams across a distributed operating footprint.
+ Set clear priorities, decision rights, performance expectations, and escalation responsibilities.
+ Strengthen capability through workforce planning, succession, cross-training, field exposure, and knowledge transfer.
+ Make timely decisions that balance safety, operational impact, cybersecurity, user experience, cost, and long-term supportability.
+ Anticipate material risks, challenge assumptions, and present clear recommendations to Technology and Operations leadership.

* Financial Planning, Vendor & Portfolio Support

+ Contribute to operating and capital planning for support operations, end-user technology, tools, lifecycle programs, vendors, and managed services.
+ Develop investment recommendations tied to operational continuity, productivity, risk reduction, scale, service improvement, or cost avoidance.
+ Support vendor selection, contract and renewal reviews, service-performance management, and commercial evaluations.
+ Maintain support technology roadmaps, standards, lifecycle plans, priorities, risks, and performance outcomes.
+ Maintain asset, licensing, audit, security, and records controls across assigned services.

* Stakeholder Partnership & Communication

+ Represent corporate and field support requirements in strategy, standards, projects, and investment decisions.
+ Communicate service health, incidents, risks, priorities, investments, and results to business, field, technical, and executive leaders.
+ Maintain direct engagement with corporate business leaders, operational leaders, and service partners to validate performance and identify emerging needs.

* Other duties as assigned.

**MINIMUM ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* 10+ years of progressive IT operations, enterprise support, field services, end-user support, or service delivery experience, including 5+ years leading distributed teams.
* Proven leadership of Service Desk, corporate support, and Field Services in a complex, multi-site environment; industrial or energy experience is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated success managing ownership, dependencies, changes, and incidents across Corporate IT, Field Operations, and OT.
* Ability to set strategy, execute at scale, lead change, and deliver measurable operating results.
* Operational Leadership: Delivers reliable, secure support across corporate and field operations.
* Enterprise and IT/OT Leadership: Establishes clear ownership, decision rights, and accountability across Corporate IT, business functions, Field Operations, and OT.
* Execution: Converts strategy into operating plans, clear measures, and sustained results.
* Business Judgment: Balances business needs, operational risk, cybersecurity, service, cost, and long-term supportability.
* Executive Communication: Frames issues, options, decisions, and results with clarity and credibility.
* Participate in a leadership escalation rotation for major incidents and critical technology events; this role is not the routine first-line on-call resource.
* Travel up to 25% to corporate offices, field locations, terminals, plants, operational facilities, and vendor sites.
* Comply with applicable site access, safety, personal protective equipment, and operational requirements when visiting field facilities.
* Ability to occasionally lift and move technology equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.
* Regular and reliable attendance.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Experience with enterprise ITSM, endpoint and mobile management, remote support, collaboration, asset management, and automation platforms.
* Experience supporting remote locations with limited connectivity, constrained local resources, or 24x7 operations.
* Experience supporting midstream, pipeline, terminal, plant, gathering and processing, or comparable field operations.
* Experience coordinating service providers, field deployment partners, vendor performance, and workforce capacity.
* Working knowledge of ITIL foundations, financial planning, contracts, licensing, audit controls, cybersecurity, and formal change management; relevant certifications are a plus.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY:**

We also strive to provide reasonable accommodation to employees’ beliefs and practices that do not conflict with Targa’s policies and applicable law. We value the unique contributions that every employee brings to their role with Targa.

  staff. Participates in organizational development and succession planning.

Description:
**Build your career with Ezee Fiber, proudly recognized by PCMag as the Best Overall ISP in the U.S. for 2026.**
At Ezee Fiber, you'll do more than build a career, you'll help shape the future of connectivity. Every team member plays a vital role in delivering reliable, high-speed internet and exceptional customer experiences. Whether in the field, in the office, or behind the scenes, you'll be part of a collaborative team that values innovation, professional growth, and making a meaningful impact in the communities we serve.
  
  
**OUR VALUES**
At Ezee Fiber, our success is built on delivering
**Speed, Simplicity, and Service**
in everything we do. Guided by our core values of
**Integrity, Compassion, Accountability, and Collaboration**
, we empower our employees to do the right thing, support one another, take ownership of their work, and work together to deliver exceptional experiences for our customers and the communities we serve.
  
  
**Job Summary**
Ezee Fiber is seeking a Program Manager, PMO to lead related construction projects and oversee Project Managers, PMO and Project Managers, Engineering within the Project Management Office. This role aligns construction delivery with strategic priorities, with a direct focus on cabinet delivery, network redundancy, and engineering release readiness across markets.
  
  
The Program Manager establishes program objectives, governance, integrated delivery plans, and performance measures for the construction build. The role coordinates cabinet delivery and redundancy requirements with Network Operations, and governs the engineering-to-construction handoff, including design release readiness and the commencement gate.
  
  
This individual partners with sponsors and functional leaders to resolve escalated issues and secure timely decisions in a growing telecommunications environment.
  
  
**Essential Functions**
**Program Leadership and Delivery**

* Lead and manage Project Managers, PMO, and Project Managers, Engineering, including aerial engineering, providing direction, coaching, workload coordination, and performance management.
* Manage dependencies among related construction projects and align resources, schedules, scope, and budgets with program priorities.

**Cabinet and Redundancy Program**

* Own the cabinet delivery and network redundancy schedule across markets, in partnership with Network Operations.
* Confirm that redundancy requirements are built into design and build plans before construction is released, and that Network Operations has readiness visibility for cabinets and routes.
* Escalate cabinet and redundancy gaps that could delay turnover or service to Market Leadership and executive teams.

Program Governance and Delivery Standards
  
  

* Develop and implement PMO project and program management standards, templates, and governance practices.
* Establish processes for project initiation, stage reviews, change control, reporting, risk management, and issue escalation.
* Ensure project and engineering teams follow approved PMO practices and obtain required sponsorship, funding, and delivery decisions.
* Maintain program documentation and promote consistent application of project management methodologies and lessons learned.

**PMO Performance and Continuous Improvement**

* Lead improvements to construction project workflows, project delivery tools, and coordination among project teams.
* Analyze performance trends and root causes to recommend and implement operational improvements to engineering and construction activity.
* Develop repeatable practices that support network deployment, market expansion, and effective transitions from capital approval to operational handoffs and project closure.

Program Reporting and Visibility
  
  

* Establish program dashboards and reporting that provide visibility into progress, dependencies, resources, and outcomes.
* Ensure data integrity and reporting accuracy across project management systems.
* Report program milestones, risks, budget performance, and key performance indicators to senior leadership.
* Conduct program reviews to improve forecasting, capacity planning, and delivery predictability.

Cross Functional Coordination
  
  

* Partner with executive team and engineering, construction, network operations, finance, sales, and vendor management teams to align program delivery with business priorities.
* Align internal teams and external partners on priorities, responsibilities, dependencies, and implementation plans.
* Coordinate implementation readiness, stakeholder communication, deliverable acceptance, and transfer of program outcomes to accountable business owners.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**
Directly supervise one or more employees. Carries out responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws.
  
  
**Qualifications**
**Education and Experience requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business administration, project management, engineering, or a related field.
* Eight or more years of project or program management experience, preferably within telecommunications or a related industry.
* Experience establishing program governance, project management frameworks, and consistent delivery standards.
* Demonstrated ability to manage related projects, coordinate resources and budgets, and drive measurable operational improvements.
* Strong stakeholder management, problem-solving, and written and verbal communication skills.
* Understanding of program lifecycle management, project interdependencies, benefits tracking, and coordination across business functions.
* Experience with enterprise project management tools (Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, SiteTracker, etc.).
* Proven leadership experience managing direct reports.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS**

* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification preferred.
* PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP) certification preferred.
* Program Management Professional (PgMP) certification preferred.
* Relevant operations or process improvement certification, such as Lean Six Sigma, preferred.

**Physical, Field, Or Environmental Requirements**
The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an associate to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of the job, the associate is required on a daily basis to analyze and interpret data, communicate, and remain in a stationary position for a significant amount of the workday and frequently access, input, and retrieve information from the computer and other office productivity devices. The associate is regularly required to move about the office and around the corporate campus. The associate must frequently move up to 10 pounds and occasionally move up to 25 pounds.
  
  
**TOTAL REWARDS**

* Competitive compensation package
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Paid Parental Leave
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off and other generous benefit programs
* Tuition reimbursement

Manage complex programs in global matrixed organization, assuming full responsibility for schedule, performance and budget.

* Build and maintain a global program structure to ensure the success of the overall program. This will typically include establishing a core team and multiple project and work stream teams with members from multiple technology, engineering, and functional groups from multiple geographic regions across the organization.
* Develop, or ensure development, of comprehensive project plans, establish objectives, and monitor adherence to the master plans and schedules. Secure and maintain adequate resources to enable the success of programs and projects.
* Secure and utilize external engineering, development, manufacturing and other functional resources where appropriate to address the needs of the program.
* Direct all phases of technology projects from inception through completion guided by an appropriate innovation process using structured tools, efficient processes, disciplined communication, and effective decision making.
* Interact with external customers to develop a clear understanding of their challenges and requirements as needed. Work closely with internal customers to establish a clear understanding of their functional requirements. Participate with Product Management in the development of business cases for projects within the program to ensure maximum value is created with Corning resources.

Domestic and international travel expected. The amount of travel time will vary based on the needs of the program. Estimated at 25-50%.
  
  
**Education And Experience**

* Bachelor of Science or higher in Engineering or other relevant discipline.
* Extensive experience in the management of complex, cross-functional, culturally diverse teams containing both technical and non-technology roles.
* Minimum of 7 years total of technology, development, and manufacturing and/or manufacturing engineering with project management experience.

**Required Skills**

* Demonstrated personal initiative with a track record of completing challenging business objectives.
* Ability to translate needs into relevant and actionable program requirements.
* Effective leadership, organization, and planning skills, with ability to handle changing priorities, changing requirements and ambiguity.
* Demonstrated communication, interpersonal, and influencing skills at all levels of an organization (team, peer, and executive levels) with a demonstrated ability to build relationships in a heavily matrixed, team environment.
* Ability to manage and effectively leverage a team of diverse expertise, backgrounds, cultures and styles.
* High English proficiency both written and verbal.

**Desired Skills**

* Multiple-year work experience in at least two of the following areas: Commercial, Development, Manufacturing, or Engineering.
* Six Sigma Black Belt training, experience and/or certification.
* Completion of formal project management training with further preference for Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.

**This position does not support immigration sponsorship.**
The range for this position is $155,994.00 - $214,493.00 assuming full time status. Starting pay for the successful applicant is dependent on a variety of job-related factors, including but not limited to geographic location, market demands, experience, training, and education.
  
  
**A job that shapes a life.**
**Corning offers you the total package.**
Your well-being is our priority. Our compensation and benefits package supports your health and wellness, financial aspirations, and career from day one.
  
  

* Company-wide bonuses and long-term incentives align with key business results and ensure you are rewarded when the company performs well. When Corning wins, we all win.

Title: Director, Surveys and Geomatics
Description:
Infrastructure Ontario (IO), an Ontario crown corporation, provides a wide range of services to support the Ontario government’s initiative to modernize and maximize the value of public infrastructure and realty. IO has been recognized domestically and internationally for the way it does business and the success it has had with its major projects, real estate services, infrastructure lending, commercial projects, and development mandate. IO delivers some of the most complex, ambitious commercial and land development solutions for the Province and continues to evolve and expand its capabilities to maximize its public impact and deliver on its vision of creating a connected, modern and competitive Ontario.
  
  
**Position Summary:**  
At IO, surveys and geomatics function ensures precise measurements and accurate mapping, which are essential for planning and executing infrastructure projects. This meticulous work takes form of land surveying, title searches, and application of advanced GIS tools and techniques. The Survey and Geomatics team is function with a long corporate history and hold a enterprise responsibility for managing and maintaining IO’s GIS information database and search application called GeoPortal used by ministries of Ontario Government and partner organization in the federal government.
  
The Director, Surveys and Geomatics reports works closely with other units that includes the Research Unit and the Data and Analytics Unit and other teams within IO’s Data & Knowledge Management Department. The Director provides subject matter expertise and leadership to the organization, overseeing the operational management of land survey and geomatics services. Knowledge and understanding on both domains are desirable to successful manage this function. The Director leads a team of land survey specialists, and mapping specialists. The role is both technical and operational. Hands-on technical work is expected at times. This role involves important collaboration and business services management role, requiring the individual to manage internal and external client expectations, service standards, product management and continued strategic development of the vendor managed GeoPortal accesses by thousands or users.
  
  
**What You Will Do:**  

* Manage the provision and delivery of specialized GIS, mapping, survey, and conveyance services. Provide technical advice and recommendations, supervise the design and implementation of standards, and ensure quality control.
* Develop and maintain partnerships with government ministries and agencies, secure new clients, and promote GeoPortal products and services to generate non-tax revenue for the Province of Ontario.
* Oversee the management of GIS systems and related service providers, recommend technological upgrades, and ensure data quality, access, security, and integrity.
* Prepare and manage procurement documents, negotiate licenses, and oversee service providers to ensure compliance with service level expectations. Manage the coordination, preparation, and control of the business unit’s budget.
* Develop and provide training in surveys, title search, and GIS systems for staff and users. Set performance standards, review staff performance, and participate in recruitment.
* Responsible for leading new approaches to geomatics and GIS systems to incorporate their usage throughout corporate decision-making.
* Lead the development of new GIS guidelines, specifications, and standards that set a benchmark for the industry and improve data integration and accessibility.
* Support the rollout of IO’s Underground Infrastructure Mapping Initiative, which is focused on delivering a centralized and secure digital repository for underground mapping data across the Province.

**Who You Are:**  

* University or college degree in Land Surveying, Geomatics, Physical Geography, Planning, Civil Engineering, or a related field is preferred.
* Many years of experience in surveys and geomatics, with expertise in GIS systems (hardware and software), mapping, and conveyance services. Knowledge of data management and technological systems is essential.
* Registered Land Surveyor accreditation would be a strong asset.
* Knowledge of legislation and regulations for professional surveying such as the Surveyor Act and associated regulations is an asset.
* Understanding of data management, application architecture, geospatial data standards and data quality management.
* Strong analytics skills to assess emerging technologies and evaluate business case.
* Experience in consulting or advisory skills to provide technical consulting for geospatial products and strategic guidance would be an asset.
* Experience with Digital Twin platform and mapping implementation would be an asset.
* Experiences in client relationship management and sales would be an asset
* Strong communication skills to market geospatial products to promote geomatics services would be an asset
* Experiences in product management and/or data product management would be an asset.
* Experiences in contract management, negotiation skills, financial administrative operations including budget development and asset management would be assets.
* Experience in leading multi-year strategic business program and services plan.
* Experience in planning, coordinating or managing IT procurement would be an asset.
* Strong leadership and team management skills, especially in service operations, excellent communication and presentation abilities, and a deep understanding of geomatics frameworks and industry practices.
* Experience with developing unit training programs and development roadmaps.
* Knowledge of public sector policies (Ontario or federal) and data governance practices, including data privacy, is an asset.

**What We Offer:**  

* Commitment to creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive culture that promotes a sense of belonging and represents and reflects the needs of the communities we serve.
* A Defined Contribution Pension Plan, with Infrastructure Ontario contributing the equivalent of 5% of a full-time employee’s annual salary and will also match any employee contribution up to an additional 5% of their annual salary. To provide further options for planning and saving for the future, IO offers a Group Retirement Savings Plan and Group Tax Free Savings Account to eligible employees.

* A pregnancy and parental leave program that offers expecting, eligible employees a top-up to 95% of their annual base salary for 31 weeks, and our parental leave program offers eligible employees a top-up to 95% of their annual base salary for 15 weeks.
* Access to our $1000 Healthcare Spending Account to top up expenses not covered in the benefits program and a Lifestyle Account that expands the eligibility of health and wellness options and can include coverage for gym memberships and fitness equipment, nutrition counselling or financial planning.

IO will also cover the costs associated with up to two membership and license fees per year for eligible colleagues if directly related to the employee’s role.

Title: Senior Manager, AI and Emerging Technology sourcing
Description:
Requisition ID: 264683
  
  
Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

  

Join Scotiabank at a pivotal time of transformation, where Procurement is driving strategic value and innovation. As the Bank accelerates its adoption of AI and digital capabilities, you’ll play a key role in shaping the future of sourcing within a global organization.

  

**The Role**

  

Shape the future of Technology Sourcing at Scotiabank

  

Scotiabank's Procurement function is at a pivotal moment — driving strategic value, commercial discipline, and innovation as the Bank accelerates its digital and AI transformation. As Senior Manager, Technology Sourcing, you'll lead high-impact sourcing strategies across some of the Bank's most complex and fastest-evolving technology categories.

  

You'll partner with Technology, Risk, Legal, Finance, and senior business leaders to unlock enterprise value across SaaS, cloud & hyperscalers, infrastructure, software, IT labour, networks, and emerging tech. This is a role for a commercially sharp procurement leader who thrives on solving complex problems, influencing spend decisions, and delivering measurable outcomes beyond savings.

  

**Is this role right for you? In this role you will:**

  

* Lead end-to-end sourcing for enterprise technology categories from opportunity assessment and market intelligence through negotiation, contracting, and benefits realization.
* Build category strategies across SaaS, cloud, software licensing, IT professional services, infrastructure, and telecom anchored in spend analysis, supplier capability, and market trends.
* Design and run competitive events (RFI/RFP/RFQ), including evaluation frameworks, shortlisting, negotiation strategy, and award recommendations.
* Negotiate commercially strong agreements balancing TCO, consumption vs. subscription models, service levels, flexibility, exit rights, and long-term business needs.
* Optimize the existing portfolio: identify renewal, consolidation, license rationalization, and vendor rationalization opportunities.
* Partner with Third-Party Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Finance to ensure alignment with policy, regulatory expectations, and the Bank's risk appetite.
* Manage strategic supplier relationships — performance, escalations, executive engagement, and continuous improvement.
* Track and report pipeline, benefits, milestones, and commitments with discipline and transparency.
* Act as a trusted advisor to Technology stakeholders and an escalation point on commercial and supplier matters with enterprise impact.

**Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We’d love to work with you if you have:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Finance, or related; CPSM, CIPS, or equivalent is preferred.
* 5–10+ years of progressive experience in strategic sourcing, category management, or supplier management — with meaningful exposure to technology categories.
* Deep familiarity with SaaS pricing models, cloud consumption economics, software licensing (perpetual, subscription, token-based), IT labour rate cards, and MSA/SOW constructs.
* Strong commercial acumen and negotiation capability, backed by data-driven recommendations.
* Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders (VP/SVP) and lead cross-functional teams through ambiguity.
* Hands-on with spend analytics, supplier segmentation, TCO modelling, and benchmarking .
* Understanding of third-party risk and regulatory expectations in financial services (or another regulated environment) is an asset.
* Familiarity with e-sourcing, CLM, and supplier management platforms.

  

**What’s in it for you?**

  

* A rewarding career path with diverse opportunities for professional development
* An organization committed to making a difference in our communities – for you and our customers.
* A competitive rewards program includes annual bonus, flexible vacation, personal and sick days, and comprehensive benefits that start on your first day.

Title: Director of IT Operations
Description:
At DC BLOX, we’re shaping the future of digital infrastructure. Our mission is to empower businesses with robust, secure, and reliable solutions that enable them to thrive in an increasingly connected world.
  
  
Founded on the principles of innovation, integrity, and customer-centricity, DC BLOX provides cutting-edge colocation, cloud services, and network solutions tailored to our clients' unique needs.
  
  
Our team is made up of passionate professionals dedicated to excellence. We foster a collaborative and inclusive workplace culture where every voice is valued and innovation is encouraged. Whether you’re an experienced industry veteran or just starting your career, DC BLOX offers a range of opportunities for growth and development.
  
  
**Description Summary**
DC BLOX is seeking a business-minded technology leader to direct IT operations, strengthen enterprise capabilities, and help shape the company’s technology strategy as the business grows. The Director of IT Operations will lead enterprise platforms, end-user services, and business application support while partnering with leaders across corporate offices, construction projects, and data center sites.
  
  
The ideal candidate combines operational depth with strategic judgment, financial discipline, and the ability to connect technology investments to business outcomes. This leader will build strong teams, establish scalable operating practices, and translate business priorities into a practical technology roadmap. The role requires a player-coach who can guide complex decisions and critical incidents while developing the team’s ability to execute independently.
  
  
This opportunity is intended for a leader with the ambition and demonstrated potential to assume broader enterprise technology leadership responsibilities. Growth will depend on performance, demonstrated readiness, and evolving business needs.
  
  
**Essential Duties**

* Shape technology strategy: Partner with the SVP, IT and business leaders to develop and execute a multiyear technology roadmap aligned with company growth, operational requirements, risk, and financial priorities.
* Lead reliable IT operations: Own enterprise platforms, infrastructure services, end-user support, and business application support, establishing clear accountability for service availability, performance, and employee experience.
* Build organizational capability: Lead and develop platform professionals, service delivery teams, application specialists, and business-facing subject matter experts. Establish clear goals, coach emerging leaders, and build succession plans that support a growing organization.
* Serve as a business partner: Work with Finance, Construction, Sales, HR, Data Center Operations, and other functions to understand business needs, improve workflows, and prioritize technology initiatives with measurable value.
* Guide technology investments: Develop business cases and recommendations that explain expected benefits, total cost of ownership, implementation requirements, and risk. Balance immediate operational needs with long-term scalability and maintainability.
* Manage financial performance and partners: Develop and manage operating and capital budgets within the role’s scope. Oversee vendors, licensing, contracts, and service providers, holding partners accountable for quality, cost, and business outcomes.
* Strengthen enterprise platforms: Oversee the availability, security, performance, integration, and lifecycle management of Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Windows Server, endpoints, virtualization, backup, monitoring, and other core technology services.
* Advance business applications and information flow: Direct support and continuous improvement of financial, construction management, CRM, HRIS, collaboration, and reporting platforms. Partner with Data and business leaders to improve integrations, data quality, and access to reliable information.
* Establish operational discipline: Mature incident, problem, request, change, asset, configuration, and knowledge management practices. Use service levels, KPIs, and trend analysis to reduce recurring issues and improve delivery.
* Strengthen resilience and risk management: Partner with Security and other stakeholders on access controls, vulnerability remediation, backup validation, disaster recovery testing, and business continuity. Communicate operational risks and remediation priorities in business terms.
* Lead scalable change: Coordinate with Project Management, Security, Data, and business stakeholders to deliver controlled production changes, clear operational handoffs, sustainable support models, and effective technology adoption.
* Evaluate innovation: Assess emerging technologies, automation, and AI-enabled capabilities for practical business use. Recommend adoption where benefits, costs, security, and support requirements justify investment.
* Communicate at the executive level: Present service performance, investment recommendations, roadmap progress, and material risks to senior leadership. Make clear recommendations and explain tradeoffs to technical and nontechnical audiences.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Education/Training/Experience**

* 10+ years of progressive experience across IT operations, enterprise platforms, infrastructure, business applications, or technology delivery, including at least 5 years leading technical teams and increasingly complex responsibilities.
* Demonstrated ability to translate business strategy into technology priorities, roadmaps, operating plans, and measurable results.
* Proven success building and developing multidisciplinary teams, delegating effectively, and establishing accountability beyond individual technical contributions.
* Experience developing and managing technology budgets, evaluating investment proposals, negotiating vendor agreements, and making decisions based on business value, cost, and risk.
* Strong technical judgment across Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Active Directory, Windows Server, endpoint management, virtualization, backup and recovery, monitoring, identity management, and enterprise security practices.
* Experience overseeing business applications and integrations. Familiarity with Sage Intacct, Kahua, Salesforce, HRIS or payroll systems, and reporting platforms is preferred.
* Demonstrated success improving IT service management, operational metrics, platform lifecycle planning, disaster recovery, and service delivery in a growing organization. Familiarity with ITIL practices is highly desirable.
* Strong understanding of how enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, data governance, and business continuity influence technology decisions; experience partnering with the leaders responsible for these areas.
* Excellent executive communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to influence across functions, resolve competing priorities, and present clear recommendations to senior leadership.
* Evidence of readiness for broader technology leadership through expanded responsibilities, cross-functional initiatives, organizational development, and sound judgment in complex situations.
* Experience in data centers, construction, critical infrastructure, or another capital-intensive, multisite business is preferred.
* Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience considered. An advanced degree or relevant ITIL, Microsoft, Azure, security, or project management certifications is a plus.

Title: Director, Technical Operations
Description:
**Who We Are**
Accommodations Plus International (API) is a technology and services company focused on driving innovation across the travel and transportation industry. We partner with organizations in the airline, cruise, and rail sectors to deliver solutions that improve layover operations, enhance customer experience, and support long-term growth.

Today, API’s platform powers over 18 million crew room nights each year for 100+ airlines and travel operators worldwide. Our Global Reach ensures that airline crews are rested, transported, and connected so global aviation runs on time.
  
  
At API, we’re building a culture rooted in succeeding and thriving together. It’s a place where people are encouraged to take ownership, develop their skills, and contribute to work that matters.
  
  
If you’re looking to grow your career in a company that values steady progress, real impact, and long-term development, we’d like to meet you!
  
  
**Summary/Objective**
The Director of Technical Operations is a senior IT leader responsible for the reliability, performance, and continuous improvement of API's internal technology environment. This leader oversees all aspects of corporate IT operations, including helpdesk and end-user support, employee hardware lifecycle management, corporate systems administration, enterprise AI tooling ownership, and the tools and processes that keep our global workforce productive every day. Operating across teams in Canada, India, Brazil, and the United States, the Director will lead a team of approximately [X] employees, including [X] direct reports, and manage and develop geographically distributed IT support and systems teams, setting clear service standards and fostering a culture of responsiveness, accountability, and employee-first service delivery. This role requires a seasoned IT operations leader who brings deep experience in enterprise support environments, strong people management skills, and the ability to align internal technology services with the needs of a growing, globally distributed organization.
  
  
**Essential Functions**
**Reasonable**
*****accommodations*****
**may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.**
****Leadership & Team Management****

* Lead, mentor, and develop distributed IT operations teams across Canada, India, Brazil, and the US, fostering a collaborative, service-oriented culture that bridges time zones and delivers a consistent employee experience globally
* Define team structure, staffing levels, roles, and career development frameworks for helpdesk technicians, desktop support engineers, and systems administrators across Canada, India, Brazil, and the US
* Establish clear goals, KPIs, and performance expectations for the IT operations organization; conduct regular performance reviews and provide ongoing coaching and feedback
* Partner with HR and talent acquisition to recruit and retain skilled IT support professionals in Canada, India, Brazil, and the US; build a team capable of scaling to meet growing organizational demand
* Foster a customer-service culture within the IT team, setting expectations for responsiveness, communication quality, and employee satisfaction across all support interactions
* Facilitate cross-functional collaboration between IT operations and HR, Finance, Legal, and business teams to anticipate technology needs and deliver solutions proactively

****Helpdesk & End-User Support****

* Own the global helpdesk function end-to-end, including service desk operations, ticket management, escalation procedures, SLA definitions, and performance reporting for teams in Canada, India, Brazil, and the US
* Administer the helpdesk ticketing and knowledge management tools used by the global support team, ensuring workflows, categorization, and reporting meet organizational needs
* Define and enforce helpdesk SLAs and response time targets; monitor queue performance, ticket aging, and resolution rates, and drive continuous improvement initiatives to reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR)
* Establish and maintain a comprehensive, searchable knowledge base and self-service portal to reduce repeat ticket volume and empower employees to resolve common issues independently
* Oversee Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 support workflows, ensuring clear escalation paths and effective knowledge transfer between support levels
* Develop and report on helpdesk metrics and employee satisfaction scores (CSAT) to executive leadership; use data to identify systemic issues and prioritize improvements
* Manage on-call and after-hours support coverage across time zones to ensure critical support needs are addressed outside standard business hours

****Employee Hardware & Asset Management****

* Own the full lifecycle of employee hardware including procurement, provisioning, deployment, tracking, maintenance, refresh, and secure decommissioning for laptops, desktops, mobile devices, peripherals, and other end-user equipment
* Develop and maintain a hardware refresh strategy and multi-year capital plan, ensuring employees in Canada, India, Brazil, and the US are equipped with current, standardized, and reliable devices

Title: Vertical Operations Director
Description:
